source.label: thm:fed_lower
source.quote: For any consistent algorithm $\Pi$, the regret $R(T)$ in Eqn.~\eqref{eqn:regret_personal} can be lower bounded as \liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{R_{\Pi}(T)}{\log(T)}\geq \sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{k\neq k'_{*,m}}\max\{...\}, where $Y_{k,m}=(\alpha+\frac{1-\alpha}{M})X_{k,m}+\mu'_{k,m}-(\alpha+\frac{1-\alpha}{M})\mu_{k,m}$ and $Z^m_{k,n}=\frac{1-\alpha}{M}X_{k,m}+\mu'_{k,n}-\frac{1-\alpha}{M}\mu_{k,m}$.

results.notes: Complex instance constant encoded as declared symbol LB_1. Paper notes the bound is not universally tight in alpha.

symbols.sum_mk: sum over clients m in [M] and arms k != k'_{*,m} (client m's mixed-model optimal arm)

source.label: col:fed_lower_gaussian
source.quote: For any consistent algorithm $\Pi$, if the rewards follow Gaussian distributions with unit variance, the regret is lower bounded as \liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{R_{\Pi}(T)}{\log(T)}\geq \sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{k\neq k'_{*,m}}\max\{\frac{2\beta^2}{\Delta'_{k,m}}, \frac{2\gamma^2\Delta'_{k,m}}{(\Delta'_{k})^2}\}, where $\beta = \alpha+\frac{1-\alpha}{M}$, $\gamma = \frac{1-\alpha}{M}$ and $\Delta'_{k}=\min_{n:k'_{*,n}\neq k}\Delta'_{k,n}$.

results.notes: Gaussian unit variance special case of Theorem 1.

symbols.R_glob: sum_m sum_{k != k'_{*,m}} Delta'_{k,m} sum_{p=1}^{p'_k} ceil((1-alpha) f(p)) (global exploration loss)
